headline: Telecoms eye space. Acquisitions abound. Funding flows.
deck: This week, telecoms and defense firms are making moves in space, while funding rounds continue to pour in.

stories.head: MDA Space pays $620 million for Blue Canyon
stories.body: MDA Space has announced its acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies for $620 million, aiming to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S. market. This deal underscores MDA's ambition to penetrate the lucrative small satellite sector, which has seen increasing demand from both commercial and defense customers. As the market for satellite technology heats up, MDA is betting that buying in is better than building from scratch.
stories.soWhat: Buying Blue Canyon might just be MDA's way of admitting that organic growth in this sector is a slow march through molasses.

stories.head: ElevationSpace raises $40 million amid transport hype
stories.body: ElevationSpace has secured $40 million in Series B funding, bringing its total to $63.5 million. The company is focused on space transportation, a sector that remains a hot topic despite the fact that many rockets are still more concept than reality. The funding reflects a continued appetite for investment in transportation solutions, even if the market is still figuring out its long-term viability.
stories.soWhat: Investors seem to be betting that the transportation hype will eventually translate into actual launches, but it feels more like a game of musical chairs.

stories.head: Palantir extends TITAN program by $480 million
stories.body: Palantir has received a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, reinforcing its position in the defense tech space. This contract extension highlights the growing reliance on sophisticated data analytics for military operations, as the DoD continues to prioritize advanced technology solutions. Palantir's persistence in securing government contracts suggests a strategic focus on long-term relationships rather than one-off projects.
stories.soWhat: In government contracting, it seems that long-term relationships are more lucrative than a flashy new product launch.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Jio's LEO plans
watchlist.body: Jio Platforms' sovereign LEO constellation plan could shake up the telecom space, especially if they successfully navigate the IPO waters.

watchlist.title: Northrop Grumman's solid rocket ambitions
watchlist.body: With claims of scaling solid rocket production, Northrop Grumman's next steps will reveal whether talk translates to action.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser launch
watchlist.body: After clearing its critical design review, the real test will be whether Dream Chaser can actually launch without a hitch.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C implications
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding could signal increased interest in co-orbital security solutions among defense contractors.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
